NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice delivers magnetic_gradient_separation using a static magnetic field to extract ferrous contaminants; our departure is a pulsed high-gradient magnetic field with synchronized flow modulation to selectively capture and release paramagnetic boron-magnesium complexes without permanent entrapment. This works because boron-magnesium impurities form weakly paramagnetic colloids that respond to transient field changes but not static fields, exploiting their unique magnetic susceptibility contrast.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: F = χV(μ₀/2)B∇B (magnetic gradient force on paramagnetic particle). Magnitude verification: Assume χ = 1e-5 (boron-magnesium colloidal complex), B = 1.5 T, ∇B = 1000 T/m, V = 1e-12 m³ (1 μm particle), μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ N/A². F = (1e-5)(1e-12)(4π×10⁻⁷/2)(1.5)(1000) ≈ 9.4×10⁻¹⁵ N > thermal noise (kT ≈ 4×10⁻²¹ N·m at 300 K), sufficient for capture.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Components: Pulsed electromagnet coil (copper, 100 turns, 0.5 m diameter), flow modulator (pneumatic valve, 10 ms response), control unit (PLC with pulse generator), stainless-steel separation chamber (0.2 m³ volume).
- Materials: Boron-nitride coil former (chemically inert), titanium electrodes (corrosion-resistant).
- Instruments: ALREADY-RECORDED flow_rate sensor (stated: "flow transducer"), ALREADY-RECORDED pressure sensor (stated: "pressure transducer"), ALREADY-RECORDED brine composition analyzer (stated: "ICP-MS telemetry").
- Procedure: Install chamber in brine line upstream of extraction; modulate flow at 5 Hz (pulse width 50 ms) synchronized with 0.5 s electromagnet pulses.
- References: DERIVED from stated spec: Pulse frequency = 1/(2×residence_time) = 1/(2×30 s) = 0.033 Hz (CALCULATED from stated "residence time: 30 s"). DERIVED threshold: B_min = √(2kT/(χVμ₀∇B)) = 0.8 T (CALCULATED from physics and ASSUMED particle size 1 μm).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installability: Same as standard magnetic separator (bolt-in chamber, compatible with existing piping).
- Operability: Adds PLC programming complexity but no new operator training (standard practice already uses magnetic separators).
- Maintenance: Comparable (coil replacement interval similar to static magnets; no consumables).
- Cost class: Same as standard practice (electromagnet vs. permanent magnet; negligible difference).
- Conclusion: Same burden class, different mechanism.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
- Protocol: Run separation chamber for 48 hours with pulsed field (0.5 s on, 0.5 s off); measure boron/magnesium in outflow via ALREADY-RECORDED ICP-MS telemetry every 15 minutes.
- Pass/Fail Threshold: Impurity reduction ≥70% (vs. baseline) sustained for 1 hour.
- Duration: 48 hours continuous.
- Kill Criterion: Mechanism is falsified if impurity reduction <70% within 48 hours or if pressure drop exceeds stated "max allowable: 50 kPa" (ALREADY-RECORDED spec).

CONSTRAINT BIND — Primary stated indicator is "boron/magnesium impurities degrade battery-grade product" (per failure definition). Secondary indicator (pressure drop) supplements but does not replace primary.
